extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, journal editors, and reviewer trainers (scholars interested in the epistemology of peer review)
extracted.subtask_description: Philosophically grounded norms and evaluative criteria for academic peer review derived from Michael Polanyi's writings on tacit knowledge and personal judgement, aimed at informing how reviewers should judge manuscripts. Emphasises the irreducibility of tacit judgement, the necessity of personal commitment, and operational norms for responsible reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connoisseurship
rubrics_metrics.description: The trained capacity to recognise quality in the discipline. Acquired through apprenticeship rather than by following explicit rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connoisseurship cannot be replaced by checklists alone; it is the pattern-recognition, taste, and disciplinary judgement that enable a reviewer to spot quality that formal criteria may miss. Be aware that connoisseurship can also generate conservatism (see tensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to the standards of the discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of the field's existing standards as a precondition for criticism: reviewers operate from a shared disciplinary framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not blind obedience; it means criticism should engage the field's standards as the background against which novelty is judged. Reviewers should state when they are invoking these standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of valid problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to distinguish a genuine scientific or scholarly question from a pseudo-question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good reviewers identify whether a manuscript addresses a meaningful problem for the discipline rather than merely presenting noise or rhetorical novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual responsibility (stake your judgement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Willingness to take a definite position and defend it; reviewers must 'stake' their judgement rather than offering evasive lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear recommendation (accept/revise/reject) and a reasoned defence; avoid only enumerating concerns without committing to an overall judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity (honesty about limits of one's knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honesty about the limits of one's own competence and knowledge when evaluating work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explicitly acknowledge where their expertise ends instead of claiming universal competence; this helps editors interpret the reviewer's authority and reduces overreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of reception
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity to recognise novel contributions whose value is not yet articulated by the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be prepared to see and value departures from received categories and to explain why a new direction is promising even when its contribution is not yet fully formed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of tacit knowledge ('We can know more than we can tell')
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that scientific evaluation involves tacit pattern-recognition, taste, and instincts that cannot be fully expressed as explicit criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that some epistemic weight legitimately resides in the reviewer's narrative and tacit judgement; explicit rubrics cannot capture all dimensions of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between explicit rubrics and tacit judgement (rule-based vs tacit evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit rubrics are necessary but insufficient; review quality depends on both rule-based checks and irreducible tacit judgements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying solely on checklists. Systems that heavily limit tacit judgement (e.g., some registered-report procedures) reduce certain abuses but cannot eliminate the need for tacit judgements at key moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-check for conservatism vs originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness that connoisseurship trained on the existing field tends to undervalue genuinely novel work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should actively guard against conservative bias by asking whether a negative judgement stems from novelty being unfamiliar rather than from substantive flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polycentric evaluation (multiple, overlapping reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The republic of science is maintained by mutual evaluation: no single reviewer is competent across the entire map; multiple perspectives are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions should rely on several polycentric reviewers whose overlapping competences help aggregate reliable judgements and compensate for individual limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare the tacit standards being invoked
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational norm: reviewers should explicitly state the tacit standards or expectations they are using when making judgements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if such standards cannot be fully justified in rule form, a reviewer can write e.g. 'in my field work of this type is expected to do X' to make the implicit basis of the judgement visible to editors and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limits of one's own competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational norm: reviewers should state where their competence ends rather than pretending universality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By acknowledging limits, reviewers provide editors with a clearer sense of which aspects of the review are authoritative and where additional expert input is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reject merely because a manuscript does not fit existing categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational norm: reviewers should not dismiss work solely for failing to conform to established disciplinary categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because connoisseurship can misjudge the genuinely new, reviewers should evaluate whether category-mismatch masks substantive promise rather than using it as a default rejection reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a definite recommendation and defend it (avoid evasiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational norm: reviewers should stake a clear recommendation and provide a reasoned defence rather than offering only an inconclusive list of concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice supports editorial decision-making and aligns with Polanyi's claim that personal commitment is constitutive of evaluation.
